blinding_guess.why: All seven packet elements are declared in the public sections of the C++ headers (ActionServer in action_server.h, ServerGoalHandle in server_goal_handle.h) and have matching template definitions in the _imp.h files; the in-package tests (ref_server.cpp, server_goal_handle_destruction.cpp) and SimpleActionServer use them consistently with these signatures. Nothing in the listed elements looks broken at this revision.

notes: All elements are C++ API symbols of the header-only templates actionlib::ActionServer<ActionSpec> and actionlib::ServerGoalHandle<ActionSpec>; they are not ROS topics/services, so msg_type, frame, units, qos, rates and definition_id are null (ROS 1, and message types depend on the ActionSpec template argument). api:actionlib::ActionServer::ActionServer has five constructor overloads at this revision (action_server.h:84-87 (n, name, goal_cb, cancel_cb, auto_start); :96-98 (n, name, goal_cb, auto_start); :107-109 ROS_DEPRECATED (n, name, goal_cb, cancel_cb = boost::function<void (GoalHandle)>()); :117-118 (n, name, auto_start); :125 ROS_DEPRECATED (n, name)); declares records the first declared overload only. ActionServer::GoalHandle is a public typedef for ServerGoalHandle<ActionSpec> (action_server.h:71). The constructor/start() create topics goal, cancel (subscribed) and status, result, feedback (published) relative to the action name, which is supplied at run time; these are not packet elements. Python equivalents (actionlib.ActionServer.start, ServerGoalHandle.set_accepted/set_canceled/set_succeeded/get_goal in src/actionlib/) also exist but the packet element names are the C++ symbols. references is scoped to message types named in the headers that declare the provided elements; general roscpp/boost API usage is not enumerated. not_declared is empty because every packet element is declared.
